category_title: Adolescents with ADHD exhibiting low levels of agency, chronic procrastination, and disorganized academic behaviors
scenario_title: Managing a long-term research project and overcoming procrastination
minimal_context: The student is sitting down to work on a four-page research assignment the day before it is due.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Let's look at your four-page research assignment. You have the instruction sheet and rubric here, and it needs to be completed.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: I started thinking about it pretty much right away when we got the sheet, but I haven't done the actual work. I guess I'm just lazy when it comes to tasks that take sustained mental effort.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: What are some ways you might improve your progress on this assignment?

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: I mean, if I could just be more organized and do not procrastinate... Like, I just... like, I'll sit home... I've got, like, a four-page thing due in two days and I say I'm going to get it done, then next thing I know, it's 12:00 the day before and I don't have it done yet.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Well, it is due tomorrow. Go ahead and start writing the four pages now.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: I can't, I'm completely daunted by the scope of this project! I started freaking out because it's 4 a.m., and it's due the next day, and I have no idea what I wrote... 'cause it's so late... so I burst out into tears and I ran downstairs and I was, like, crying to my mom.

task.content: Managing long-term projects and research assignments, such as a four-page assignment

context.environment: Responding to long-term assignments after receiving the instruction sheet/rubric
context.social_setting: Working independently at home or in a tutoring session
context.time_context: 12:00 the day before it is due, or 4 a.m. the day it is due

challenging_behavior_trigger.condition: being daunted by the scope of a project and tasks that involve sustained mental effort
challenging_behavior_trigger.observable_behavior: procrastinate on the actual work and end up rushing to complete assignments by their deadlines, burst out into tears, crying to my mom
challenging_behavior_trigger.internal_state: freaking out because it’s 4 a.m., and it’s due the next day, and I have no idea what I wrote
related_quotes: I started freaking out because it’s 4 a.m., and it’s due the next day, and I have no idea what I wrote … ’cause it’s so late … so I burst out into tears and I ran downstairs and I was, like, crying to my mom.

Like, I just … like, I’ll sit home … I’ve got, like, a four-page thing due in two days and I say I’m going to get it done, then next thing I know, it’s 12:00 the day before and I don’t have it done yet.

behavior_patterns.condition: When specifically prompted with a question regarding ways they might improve their grades
behavior_patterns.observable_behavior: suggested ideas such as do not procrastinate, complete work, be more organized... but they did not embrace these ideas as things they would implement; used words such as 'if' and 'I could,' suggesting these were hypothetical plans
behavior_patterns.internal_state: Not one student was convinced his or her grades would improve if he or she were to study more
